data_point_breakdown.unified_benchmarks: 17 sources, 36 synthetic runs, 3 live tests, 2880 coord measurements, 146 data-gathering points = 3065
data_point_breakdown.empirical_benchmarks: 7 categories, 10 team-size configs, 6 contention configs, 4 pipeline configs, 2 connection patterns, 45 tool tests = 67
data_point_breakdown.think_tank_convergence: 30 team logs, 155 stress tests, 7 benchmark categories = 192 (meta-analyzed)

optimal_team_size.verdict: 5-8 agents per team for task execution. Solo (1) for research. Never exceed 15 without unique-per-agent justification.

evidence.power_law: E = 4.0 * N^(-0.75). Every doubling of team size reduces per-agent output by 40-50%.
evidence.cross_reference_insight: Infrastructure overhead is <1% at ALL sizes (empirical). The 89% efficiency loss at 16+ agents is cognitive, not mechanical: context-switching, communication ambiguity, and work duplication dominate. This means infrastructure optimization alone cannot fix large-team inefficiency.

optimal_team_size.curve_methodology: Power law E=4.0*N^(-0.75) calibrated to historical data, validated against empirical overhead: at N=8, predicted E=0.76 vs observed TEAM-0024 at 12.0 (parallel-test outlier) and TEAM-0018 at 1.0 (parallel-build). The power law represents median expectation; pattern selection causes 15x variance.
optimal_team_size.recommendation: Default to 5-8 agents per team. Use solo agents for research tasks (5.5x efficiency). The overhead curve flattens at 8 agents (4.2ms/agent) but historical efficiency craters at 9+ (0.36 mean). The binding constraint is cognitive, not infrastructure.

optimal_connections.verdict: Hybrid architecture: hub for coordination/status, channels for inter-agent messaging under concurrent load.

hub_vs_channels.proto_b_live_throughput: 82% of baseline (FIFO+mmap has higher fixed cost)

optimal_connections.when_to_use_hub: Agent registration, status reporting, coordinator dashboard reads, instruction broadcast, idle detection (0.04ms median). Any operation where a single writer (coordinator) reads/writes and latency p95 <2ms is acceptable.
optimal_connections.when_to_use_channels: Inter-team messaging under concurrent load (8+ simultaneous senders), progress broadcasting to multiple consumers, any scenario where >4 threads write simultaneously. Channels keep p95 at 55ms vs hub's 105ms under 8-10 thread contention.
optimal_connections.recommendation: Deploy hub-and-spoke for coordinator operations and agent status. Use direct channels for team-to-team communication when concurrent messaging is expected. Communication overhead is negligible (<0.05% of runtime) regardless of pattern chosen.

optimal_order_of_operations.verdict: Parallel-first with 3-phase structure. Pipelines only for tasks with true stage dependencies, capped at 5-10 stages.

pipeline_stages_analysis.scaling: Linear. Per-stage overhead is stable at 0.88-1.07ms. No nonlinear bottleneck up to 20 stages.
pipeline_stages_analysis.optimal_depth: 5-10 stages. Per-stage cost minimizes at 5 (0.88ms) and stays low through 10 (0.94ms). Beyond 10, per-stage cost rises slightly and total overhead exceeds 10ms.

parallel_vs_sequential.ratio: Parallel patterns average 4.57x efficiency. Sequential patterns average 0.15x. Parallel is 30x better on average.
parallel_vs_sequential.why_sequential_fails: Wave-sequential and 8-team-pipeline introduce idle time. Agents waiting for upstream stages do zero useful work. Historical data shows 0.125-0.176 efficiency for sequential vs 1.0-12.0 for parallel.

optimal_order_of_operations.phase_structure: 3 phases: (1) Research & Discovery [solo agents, parallel], (2) Build & Implement [small teams, parallel-build + work stealing], (3) Test & Validate [parallel-test, partitioned suites]. Run think-tank convergence after each phase, not just at end.
optimal_order_of_operations.recommendation: Maximize parallelism within each phase. Use pipelines ONLY for true dependencies (e.g., build-then-test for the same module). Keep pipelines to 5-10 stages max. Never serialize work that can be parallelized - it costs 30x in efficiency.

optimal_agent_to_subagent_ratio.verdict: 2-4 subagents per coordinating agent (SQLite database). The efficiency cliff is at 4 concurrent writers; beyond 8, throughput collapses.
optimal_agent_to_subagent_ratio.efficiency_cliff: 4 concurrent writers. At 4 threads, throughput drops to 36% of single-thread and p99 latency hits 34ms. At 8 threads, only 16% throughput remains. The p50 latency stays constant at ~0.24ms across all thread counts - the problem is SQLite WAL write serialization causing extreme tail latency.
optimal_agent_to_subagent_ratio.cross_reference_with_team_size: The empirical overhead data shows team sizes of 5-8 have optimal per-agent overhead (4.2-4.5ms). Combined with the 4-thread contention cliff, this means a coordinator with 3-4 subagents per shared database is optimal. For 8 agents, use 2 databases or 2 sub-coordinators each managing 4 writers.

thundering_herd_data.note: Work stealing is safe (no double-claims) but thundering herd adds 120x tail latency. Use single-consumer pattern when possible.

optimal_agent_to_subagent_ratio.recommendation: Limit to 2-4 concurrent writers per SQLite database. For teams of 5-8, partition into 2 write groups or use a single-writer coordinator pattern. Beyond 4 writers, each additional writer yields only marginal throughput gain while p99 latency escalates rapidly. For >16 agents, increase _MAX_RETRIES from 5 to 10.

ranked.detail: 64.6% denial rate in synthetic benchmarks. Proto A throughput collapsed to 20.9% of baseline (31.78 vs 157.38 dp/s). Live tests showed 0% denials at 3 agents - the rate limiter is misconfigured for scale, not fundamentally broken.
ranked.impact: Blocks production use beyond 3 agents. Single biggest performance bottleneck.
ranked.fix: Recalibrate rate limiter thresholds. Current settings are ~5x too aggressive for multi-team scenarios.

ranked.detail: 96% throughput reduction from 1 to 32 threads (3230 to 120 ops/s). p99 latency >130ms at 16 threads.
ranked.impact: Hard scaling ceiling at ~15 concurrent writers. Beyond this, coordination becomes the bottleneck instead of the work.
ranked.fix: Partition databases by team. Use single-writer coordinator pattern. Increase retry budget for large deployments.

ranked.detail: No timeout-based reclaim for in_progress work items. A crashed agent permanently blocks its assigned work.
ranked.impact: Can silently deadlock pipelines. Risk increases with team size and operation duration.
ranked.fix: Add timeout-based reclaim (default 30min). Mark stale items as available after timeout.

ranked.detail: JSONL bus files grow unbounded at ~318 bytes/datapoint. Proto A generated 2MB across 12 runs. At 50 agents, files could reach 10MB+ per session.
ranked.impact: Read amplification (7.5x observed in Proto A). Startup time degrades as bus files grow.
ranked.fix: Implement bus file rotation at >1MB. Archive old segments.

ranked.detail: Bus read offsets are in-memory only. Lost on agent restart, causing message re-processing.
ranked.impact: Duplicate work after any restart. Compounds with bus file growth.
ranked.fix: Persist read offsets to SQLite. Restore on restart.

ranked.detail: S4 scenario (inject_failure=true) produced zero errors across all prototypes. Failure injection is non-functional.
ranked.impact: Cannot validate fault tolerance. Unknown behavior under real failures.
ranked.fix: Debug and fix failure injection in benchmark harness.

ranked.detail: No automatic TTL enforcement for scratchpad entries.
ranked.impact: Disk accumulation over time. Minor at current scale.

fixes_needed_before_scaling: FIX RATE LIMITER: Recalibrate thresholds to eliminate 64.6% denial rate (blocks all scaling)
ADD ZOMBIE RECLAIM: Timeout-based work item reclaim at 30min default (prevents pipeline deadlocks)
IMPLEMENT BUS ROTATION: Compact/rotate at >1MB (prevents read amplification at scale)
PERSIST READ OFFSETS: Store in SQLite, not memory (prevents duplicate work after restart)
INCREASE RETRIES: Raise _MAX_RETRIES from 5 to 10 for deployments with >16 concurrent writers

cross_cutting_insights.insight: The 79.1% Proto A throughput collapse in synthetic tests vs 2.5% GAIN in live tests reveals the rate limiter is the sole cause of poor synthetic performance. Live tests at 3 agents show zero denials. The rate limiter is misconfigured for scale, not fundamentally flawed.
cross_cutting_insights.implication: Fixing the rate limiter alone would likely bring Proto A synthetic throughput to 95%+ of baseline, matching Proto B.

cross_cutting_insights.insight: Infrastructure overhead is <1% at ALL team sizes (empirical: 0.35-0.74%), yet historical efficiency drops 89% from solo to 16+ agents. The binding constraint on team performance is cognitive overhead (context-switching, communication ambiguity, work duplication), not infrastructure latency.
cross_cutting_insights.implication: Investing in faster coordination primitives will NOT improve team efficiency. Investing in better task partitioning, clearer work specifications, and deduplication detection WILL.

cross_cutting_insights.insight: Pattern selection causes 96x variance in efficiency (parallel-test at 12.0 vs 8-team-pipeline at 0.125). Team size causes only 17x variance (solo at 5.5 vs xlarge at 0.32). Choosing the right cooperation pattern matters 5.6x more than choosing the right team size.
cross_cutting_insights.implication: Optimizing for team size alone captures <20% of available efficiency gains. Pattern selection is the primary lever.

cross_cutting_insights.insight: The SQLite contention cliff at 4 threads (36% efficiency) combined with the team-size sweet spot at 5-8 agents creates an architectural tension. A team of 8 agents all writing to one DB operates at 16% throughput efficiency. Solution: 2 sub-coordinators of 4 agents each, or single-writer coordinator pattern.
cross_cutting_insights.implication: Teams of 5-8 MUST use partitioned write access or a coordinator proxy to avoid hitting the SQLite cliff.

cross_cutting_insights.insight: Token efficiency (90.2% reduction, 11.7x speedup) transforms agent session economics. An agent that previously fit ~16 index reads per context window now fits ~190. This enables previously impossible patterns: full-index search before every decision, iterative refinement loops, multi-source cross-referencing within a single session.
cross_cutting_insights.implication: All agents should use smart_read/query_kb/smart_write exclusively. Raw file I/O wastes 90% of context budget.

cross_cutting_insights.insight: Data-gathering iteration 1 to 2 showed 371% more data points, 67% quality improvement, and 400% more functional methods. The Hybrid v2 method (DG-0004) consistently wins on quality (92/100) while being only 12% slower than iteration 1. OpenAlex (0.5s) is the fastest functional academic source.
cross_cutting_insights.implication: Default to Hybrid v2 for quality-critical research. Use OpenAlex for speed-critical academic lookups. Always iterate on data-gathering methods - second iteration showed massive gains.

cross_cutting_insights.insight: Work stealing is double-steal safe (confirmed empirically with 10 threads, 50 items), but thundering herd adds 120x tail latency (p95: 79ms vs 0.66ms). Combined with the help protocol's correct race resolution (exactly 1 winner per race), the coordination primitives are production-ready for correctness but need performance tuning under contention.
cross_cutting_insights.implication: Use single-consumer work stealing when possible. Reserve multi-consumer thundering-herd scenarios for when latency p95 >80ms is acceptable.

cross_cutting_insights.insight: 7 consecutive infrastructure-focused teams (Phase 2-3) produced 'inward-facing gravity' - teams building tools for other teams rather than delivering external value. Combined with 13 SOPs approaching overhead saturation, the repo risks becoming self-referential.
cross_cutting_insights.implication: Next operations should be outward-facing: apply the optimized infrastructure to external tasks (market research, data gathering, analysis). Infrastructure work should be bug-fix only.

immediate: Fix rate limiter: Recalibrate thresholds to eliminate 64.6% denial rate. This is the #1 blocker. Expected throughput recovery: 4-5x for Proto A.
Adopt smart I/O exclusively: All agents must use query_kb, smart_read, smart_write. Saves 90% of context tokens per operation.
Set team size default to 5-8: Encode in SOP. Require justification for >8 agents per team.
Use hybrid connection pattern: Hub for coordinator ops, channels for inter-team messaging. Document as standard architecture.
short_term: Implement zombie work item reclaim (30min timeout). Required before any pipeline-based operation.
Add bus file rotation at >1MB. Prevents read amplification scaling issue.
Persist bus read offsets to SQLite. Eliminates duplicate work after restart.
Partition SQLite writes: For teams of 5+, use 2 sub-coordinators or single-writer proxy to stay under 4-thread contention cliff.
Deploy outward-facing operations: Use optimized infra for market research, data gathering, analysis tasks. Stop building more infra.
Increase _MAX_RETRIES to 10 for any deployment planning >16 concurrent writers.
long_term: Evaluate SQLite WAL alternatives for >15 concurrent writers (e.g., per-team databases with periodic merge, or move to a concurrent-write-optimized store).
Build automated pattern selector: Given task type and agent count, recommend optimal cooperation pattern. 96x variance in efficiency means pattern choice is the highest-leverage decision.
Implement adaptive rate limiting: Instead of static thresholds, use feedback-based rate control that adjusts to actual API response times and error rates.
Create real fault tolerance testing: Fix failure injection (currently non-functional) and validate behavior under agent crashes, network partitions, and resource exhaustion.
Develop context-window-aware scheduling: With 11.7x I/O efficiency, agents can handle more complex multi-step tasks. Redesign work items to be larger-grained.
Consider Proto B (FIFO+mmap) for latency-sensitive paths: 99.4% of baseline throughput with zero rate-limiter risk. Proto A's advantage is only 2.5% more data yield in live tests.

for_research_ops.connection: Hub only (single-thread ops, no concurrency needed)
for_research_ops.rationale: Solo researchers achieve 4-7x efficiency. Coordinator handles dedup and convergence. No inter-researcher communication needed.

for_build_ops.pattern: parallel-build with work stealing between teams
for_build_ops.connection: Hub for status + channels between teams for work stealing
for_build_ops.rationale: 3 builders per team stays under SQLite 4-thread cliff. Work stealing prevents idle time. Two teams can work on independent modules.

for_test_ops.pattern: parallel-test with partitioned suites and progress broadcasting
for_test_ops.connection: Hub for status + channels for progress broadcast + bottleneck detection
for_test_ops.rationale: Testing parallelizes perfectly with partitioned suites. TEAM-0024 achieved 12.0 efficiency with this exact pattern. Progress broadcasting catches stragglers.

for_mixed_ops.breakdown: 3 researchers (solo) + 2 build teams of 3 (6 total) + 4 testers + 1 coordinator
for_mixed_ops.pattern: 3-phase pipeline: Research -> Build -> Test, parallel within each phase
for_mixed_ops.connection: Hub for coordinator + channels for inter-phase handoffs + work stealing within build phase
for_mixed_ops.sqlite_partitioning: 3 databases: research-hub, build-hub, test-hub. Coordinator reads all 3. Max 4 concurrent writers per DB.
for_mixed_ops.rationale: 14 agents is the empirically-validated upper bound for productive mixed ops. 3 SQLite databases keep each under the 4-writer contention cliff. Phase structure prevents idle time via help protocol reallocation.

methodology_notes.efficiency_metric: Artifacts per agent (deliverable outputs divided by team size). Higher is better.
methodology_notes.power_law_derivation: Fit to 20 historical teams across 4 size buckets. R-squared not computed but trend is monotonically decreasing and consistent across all data sources.
methodology_notes.contention_data: Empirical benchmarks from 2026-03-11 run, corroborated by unified_benchmarks coordination data from coord_bench_results.json. Two independent measurement sets agree within 10%.

confidence_levels.team_size_recommendation: HIGH - 20 teams, 132 agents, consistent power law across all sources
confidence_levels.connection_pattern: HIGH - Direct A/B comparison with statistical significance (50+ measurements per condition)
confidence_levels.contention_cliff: HIGH - Two independent benchmark runs agree (3611 vs 3230 ops/s at 1 thread, both show cliff at 4)
confidence_levels.cooperation_patterns: MEDIUM - Some patterns have only 1 team observation (parallel-test, 8-team-pipeline). Rankings may shift with more data.
confidence_levels.weak_link_priorities: HIGH - Rate limiter issue confirmed by 3 independent think tanks with unanimous verdict
